sentences.text: Xericeps was a medium-sized pterosaur that lacked teeth, with a wingspan likely near the lower end of the 3 to 8 meter range typical for its group. The holotype specimen, which represents an adult animal, consists only of fragmented jaws measuring 173 millimeters in length.

The upturned jaw of Xericeps has a curved occluding surface when viewed from the side, and five pairs of elongated holes serving as openings for venous ducts are located along the lower edges of the jaw. The name Xericeps combines the Greek word for 'dry' referencing the Sahara Desert and the Latin suffix for 'head', alluding to its forceps-like beak.

A pair of ridges on the dorsal surface of the jaw symphysis resembles features found in Alanqa and Argentinadraco, though the shape of the ridges on Xericeps' jaw differs from those of Alanqa, a pterosaur from the same geological layers.
This species is known solely from its holotype specimen, which consists only of fragmented jaws and was originally described in 2017.
Five pairs of elongated holes, serving as openings for venous ducts, are located along the lower edges of the jaw.
British paleontologist David M. Martill purchased the holotype specimen directly at the mine site in January 2017.
Xericeps inhabited a subtropical alluvial plain characterized by rivers, deltas, and swampy lakes.
The habitat of Xericeps was shared with large theropod dinosaurs like Spinosaurus and Carcharodontosaurus, as well as the sauropod Rebbachisaurus.

A 2021 study classified Xericeps as a chaoyangopterid closely related to Argentinadraco, and subsequent analyses consistently place Xericeps within the family Alanqidae, though some sources classify Xericeps within the family Azhdarchidae.
Martill and colleagues classified Xericeps within the clade Neoazhdarchia based on the presence of foramina in the jaw, and the Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Xericeps as Neoazhdarchia.
Xericeps lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, and the time range for Xericeps is recorded as the Cenomanian, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
Researchers believe Xericeps lived between 93.9 and 113.0 million years ago during the Albian to Cenomanian ages.
The exact diet of Xericeps remains uncertain, though relatives like Alanqa appear to have specialized in hunting hard-shelled mollusks.
